A.subject: Physics
A.text: The side PQ of the frame shown in figure can slide freely. There exists a uniform magnetic field B, along the outward normal. At the moment t = 0, the field starts decreasing such that B = B₀/(1+kt), where B₀ and k are positive constants. The speed with which the side PQ should be moved, so that there is no current in the loop, is
A.sol_text:
Let the bar has moved through a distance x and its speed is v.
v = dx/dt
φ = BA = (B₀/(1+kt)) b(a+x)
Now dφ/dt = 0
⇒ ((1+kt)(dx/dt) − (a+x)(k))/(1+kt)² = 0
⇒ dx/dt = ((a+x)k)/(1+kt)
∫₀ˣ dx/(a+x) = ∫₀ᵗ kdt/(1+kt)
ln(a+x)/a) = ln(1+kt)
1 + x/a = 1+kt
x = akt
dx/dt = ak
⇒ v = ak

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A particle is projected from a tower of height 2 m above ground with speed 3 m/s. Neglect any air resistance to the particle's motion. Maximum horizontal distance (in m) from the foot of the tower where the particle can reach is (Take g = 10 m/s²)
B.sol_text:
Answer : 02.10
Solution:
In terms of speed u and angle of projection θ

R = (u cos θ) t	.....(i)
−H = (u sin θ) t − (1/2)gt²	.....(ii)

From (i) and (ii),
g²t⁴ − 4(gH + u²)t² + 4(R² + H²) = 0

For maximum range by displacement, this equation in t² must have equal roots.
⇒ (gH + u²)² = g²(R² + H²)

⇒ Range (maximum) = (4√(u² + 2gH))/g

= (3√(3² + 2×10×2))/10 = 2.1 m

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The osmotic pressure of an aqueous solution of sucrose at 303 K is 2.47 atm, the molar volume of water at this temperature is 18.10 cm³. Calculate the elevation in boiling point of this. (ΔH_vap = 539 cal/gm)
A.sol_text:
Answer : (3)
Solution:
π = CRT
2.47 = C × 0.082 × 303
C = 2.47/(0.082 × 303) = 9.94 × 10^(-2) (M)
Volume of solution = volume of solvent [as solution is quit dilute]
Number of moles of water present = 1000/18.1
Amount of water present = (1000/18.1) × 18 = 994.475 gm
m = (9.94×10^(-2))/994.475 × 10³ = 9.995 × 10^(-2)
ΔT_b = k_b × m
ΔT = (RT_b²)/(ΔH_vap × 1000) × m
= (1.98 × (373)²)/(539 × 1000) × 9.995 × 10^(-2) = 0.051 K

A.text: Three circles x² + y² + 2g_i x + 2f_i y = 0, i = 1, 2, 3 are mutually orthogonal. If Σ³₁ g_i² = 4 and Σ³₁ f_i² = 5, then the equation of the locus of centroid of the triangle formed by joining the centres of these three circles, is
A.sol_text:
Answer: (4)
Solution:
2g₁g₂ + 2f₁f₂ = 2g₂g₃ + 2f₂f₃ = 2g₃g₁ + 2f₃f₁ = 0
g₁² + g₂² + g₃² = 4, f₁² + f₂² + f₃² = 5
Let the centroid is G(h, k).
⇒ h = (g₁ + g₂ + g₃)/3, k = (f₁ + f₂ + f₃)/3
(3h)² + (3k)² = (g₁ + g₂ + g₃)² + (f₁ + f₂ + f₃)² = 4 + 5
h² + k² = 1 ⇒ Locus of G(h, k) is x² + y² = 1

A.text: If tan⁻¹(sin x) + tan⁻¹(2 cosec x) = m + n tan⁻¹((2+sin²x)/sin x), π < x < 3π/2, then m + n is equal to (where m, n are constants)

⇒ m = −π, n = −1

A.text: Three numbers a, b, c, a > b > c, whose sum is 26, form a geometric progression. If we add 1, 6 and 3 to a, b and c respectively, resulting numbers are in arithmetic progression, then the value of a is
A.sol_text:
Answer: (2)
Solution:
Let the numbers be (a/r), a, ar.
Then (a/r) + a + ar = 26
a(1/r + 1 + r) = 26 ...(i)
The new numbers after adding 1, 6 and 3 respectively
(a/r) + 1, a + 6, ar + 3 are in A.P.
⇒ ((a/r) + 1 + ar + 3) = 2(a + 6)
⇒ a[1/r + r] + 4 = 2a + 12
⇒ a(1/r - 2) = 12 - 4
⇒ a(1/r + r - 2) = 8
⇒ a(1/r + r - 1 - 3) = 8
⇒ a(1/r + r + 1) - 3a = 8
⇒ 26 - 3a = 8
⇒ -3a = 8 - 26
⇒ a = 18/3 = 6
⇒ a = 6
Using a = 6 in (i) we get
(1/r) + 1 + r = 26/6
3(r² + r + 1) = 13r
3r² + 3r + 3 - 13r = 0
3r² - 10r + 3 = 0
3r² - 9r - r + 3 = 0 ⇒ (r - 3)(3r - 1) = 0
r = 3, r = 1/3
The numbers are (6/3), 6, 6 × 3 i.e. 2, 6, 18.

A.text: A circle with fixed centre (3h, 3k) and of variable radius cuts the rectangular hyperbola x² - y² = 9a² at the points A, B, C, D. The locus of the centroid of the △ABC is given by
A.sol_text:
Let A, B, C, D have co-ordinate (x_i, y_i) i = 1, 2, 3, 4,....then
(x₁ + x₂ + x₃ + x₄)/4 = 3h/2 , ...(1)
(y₁ + y₂ + y₃ + y₄)/4 = 3k/2 ...(2)

Let the centroid of △ABC be (α, β), then
α = (x₁ + x₂ + x₃)/3, β = (y₁ + y₂ + y₃)/3

From equation (1) and (2) we get,
3α + x₄ = 6h and 3β + y₄ = 6k

But (x₄, y₄) lies on x² - y² = 9a²
(6h - 3α)² - (6k - 3β)² = 9a²
(α - 2h)² - (β - 2k)² = a²

Locus of (α, β) is (x - 2h)² - (y - 2k)² = a²

A.text: A biased coin with probability getting a head is p, (0 < p < 1), is tossed until a head appears for the first time. If the probability that the number of tosses required is even is 2/5, then p is equal to
A.sol_text:
Let X denotes the number of tosses required. Then P(X = r) = (1 - p)^(r-1) · p, for r = 1, 2, 3......

Let E denote the event that the number of tosses required is even.
Then P(E) = P[(X = 2) ∪ (X = 4) ∪ (X = 6) ∪ .......]
P(E) = P(X = 2) + P(X = 4) + P(X = 6) + ......
P(E) = (1 - p)p + (1 - p)³p + (1 - p)⁵p + ...... = (1-p)/(2-p)

But we are given that P(E) = 2/5, then we get p = 1/3.
